table.purpose: t01 appears to be a dimension/entity table (e.g. customers or accounts) keyed by col_001, with each row classified by a segment code (col_002) and a currency (col_003). It is referenced by t05 and t04, so it likely holds the master list of entities those tables point to. The exact business meaning cannot be determined from the data alone.

col_001.name: entity_id
col_001.description: Primary key of t01; a unique integer identifier (surrogate ID) for each row/entity. Referenced by t05.col_001 and t04.col_004, so it identifies the master record that those tables link to.

col_002.name: segment_code
col_002.description: Three-valued classification code: SME (26763 rows), LAM (3658), KAM (2040). SME strongly suggests a 'small and medium enterprise' customer segment; LAM and KAM are plausibly other segment codes (e.g. large/local account manager, key account manager), but their exact meanings are not evidenced.

col_003.name: currency_code
col_003.description: ISO 4217 currency code: CZK (Czech koruna, 30459 rows) and EUR (euro, 2002 rows). Indicates the currency associated with each entity.

table.purpose: t02 appears to be a product/brand-level fact table (one row per item, ~5716 rows) with a country market (Czech Republic / Slovakia) and a market segment classification. Exact business domain is unresolved, but the structure suggests products or SKUs assigned to brands (t03/t04) and price-tier segments within CZE/SVK markets. The relationship between t02 and t04 via col_001 being referenced by t04.col_006 suggests t04 is a child/detail table (e.g., sales or time-series records) pointing back to these items.

col_001.name: item_id
col_001.description: Primary key of t02; unique integer identifier for each row (item/SKU/product). Referenced by t04.col_006, so t04 rows link to these items.

col_002.name: brand_id
col_002.description: Foreign key to t03.col_001 (and matching t04.col_001), identifying the brand/manufacturer/group of the item. 233 distinct values, heavily skewed toward a few IDs (3, 2, 33, 1, 4).

col_003.name: country_code
col_003.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code: CZE (Czechia, 4836 rows) or SVK (Slovakia, 880 rows). Indicates the market/country of the item.

col_004.name: price_segment
col_004.description: Market/price positioning segment of the item: 'Premium', 'Value for money', 'Discount', 'Noname', 'Other'. Likely a price-tier or brand-positioning classification.

table.name: transaction_item
table.purpose: Line items of transactions, each row a charge/fee/product entry (fuel, tolls, services, fees) with a description; referenced by other tables (t04, t02).

col_001.name: item_id
col_001.description: Primary key, surrogate integer identifier for each transaction line item (1-630, unique).

col_002.name: item_description
col_002.description: Free-text description of the charged item or service (Czech/English/German), e.g. fuel products, tolls, service fees, card issuance, catalyst, groceries. Not a clean category code; values are heterogeneous.

table.purpose: t04 appears to be an event/transaction log: each row records an occurrence at a specific date and time over a four-day window (2012-08-23 to 2012-08-26), with several foreign keys to lookup/dimension tables (t01, t02, t03) and a monetary-looking amount. The exact business domain cannot be determined from the data alone, so the table's real-world meaning is unresolved, but its structure (surrogate PK, date, time, multiple FKs, amount) is clear.

col_001.name: id
col_001.description: Primary key of t04; a surrogate sequential identifier (1-1000, one per row). Referenced by t02.col_002.

col_002.name: event_date
col_002.description: Date of the event/transaction, stored as text in ISO format. Only four distinct dates (2012-08-23 to 2012-08-26), heavily concentrated on Aug 24-25.

col_003.name: event_time
col_003.description: Time of day of the event, stored as text in HH:MM:SS format. Combined with col_002 it gives the full timestamp of the row.

col_004.name: t01_ref
col_004.description: Foreign key referencing t01.col_001 (many-to-one). Values 96-49838 with moderate repetition. The meaning of the referenced entity is unknown without t01's contents.

col_006.name: t02_ref
col_006.description: Foreign key referencing t02.col_001 (many-to-one). Values 48-5481. The meaning of the referenced entity is unknown without t02's contents.

col_007.name: t03_ref_a
col_007.description: Foreign key referencing t03.col_001 (many-to-one). Highly skewed: value 2 accounts for ~52% of rows, 5 for ~24%, with 28 distinct values (2-352). Likely a category/type code; exact meaning depends on t03's contents.

col_008.name: t03_ref_b
col_008.description: Second foreign key referencing t03.col_001 (many-to-one), with 83 distinct values (0-264) and a right-skewed distribution. A different categorization than col_007; exact meaning depends on t03's contents.

col_009.name: amount
col_009.description: A positive decimal amount (1.76 to 5762.49, median ~354). The scale and two-decimal precision strongly suggest a monetary amount (e.g., transaction value), though currency and exact semantics are unconfirmed.

table.name: yearmonth
table.purpose: Monthly records of a monetary amount per entity (col_001) for each year-month (col_002); likely monthly balances, transactions, or account totals keyed to entities in t01. The exact business meaning of the amount is not determinable from the data alone.

col_001.name: entity_id
col_001.description: Identifier of the entity (e.g. account, customer, or contract) this monthly record belongs to; references t01.col_001 many-to-one. Not a primary key here since each id appears many times (up to ~20 rows, consistent with one row per month).

col_002.name: period_ym
col_002.description: Year and month in YYYYMM format (values span 201112 to 201311, i.e. 24 distinct months, ~21 non-null distinct values observed). Stored as VARCHAR but numeric in form.

col_003.name: amount
col_003.description: A monetary amount for the entity in that month; mostly positive (median ~1766) with a long right tail up to ~2,052,187 and some negative values down to -582,093, suggesting it may be a balance or net amount rather than a pure quantity. Currency and exact semantics (balance vs. transaction total vs. turnover) unresolved.
